questions.subject: Strategic Management
questions.subTopic: Strategy Implementation and Evaluation - Examination Problem
questions.question:
(a)Legacy Electronics Ltd. was once a market leader in consumer appliances and enjoyed a loyal customer base. However, increased competition, outdated product offerings, rising costs, and changing consumer expectations have adversely affected the company's performance. Over the past five years, the company has reported declining sales, continuous losses, and reduced market share. Several manufacturing facilities are operating inefficiently, while financial pressures have limited investment in innovation and marketing. Concerned about the organization's future, the management team is seeking a structured approach to revive the company's performance and restore sustainable profitability.
State the key problems involved and suggest the major components of an action plan that management should implement to improve the company's condition and achieve long-term recovery. (1 + 4 = 5 Marks)
questions.answer:
(a)The key problems indicating the need for a Turnaround Strategy in Legacy Electronics Ltd. are continuous losses, declining sales, reduced market share, uncompetitive/outdated products, rising costs, increased competition, changing customer expectations and inefficient manufacturing facilities . These indicate deterioration in the company’s competitive and financial position and the need to improve internal efficiency. The major components of the action plan for turnaround are: 1. Assessment of current problems: Identify the root causes and extent of damage and focus resources on areas requiring immediate corrective action. 2. Analysis and strategic planning: Assess the chances of survival, identify the viable core business , analyse strengths and weaknesses and develop a strategic plan with specific goals and functional actions. 3. Emergency action plan: Take immediate measures to reduce costs, improve working capital, restructure finances, prune unprofitable product lines and accelerate high -potential products . Positive operating cash flow should be established as quickly as possible. 4. Restructuring the business: Review the product mix, core products, facilities and markets . Inefficient facilities may be closed, and the company may withdraw from certain markets or reposition its products. Employee morale should also be strengthened through appropriate reward and compensation systems.

5. Returning to normal: Once profitability starts improving, the company should focus on introducing new products, improving customer service, increasing market share and developing alliances to achieve sustainable growth.

In addition, the turnaround should emphasize quick cost reductions, revenue generation, asset liquidation for generating cash, better internal coordination and, where necessary, changes in top management.

questions.subject: Strategic Management
questions.subTopic: Strategic Analysis: Internal Environment - Examination Problem
questions.question: (b)NewGlow Herbals, a company producing premium herbal cosmetics, sold their products mainly through large supermarket chains and online retail platforms. Recently the company started facing pressure from major retailers who demanded a reduction of prices. They argue that since customers are highly price sensitive they would have to replace NewGlow Herbals products with cheaper alternative brands. In order to stay competitive, NewGlow Herbals though reluctant, was forced to reduce the maximum retail prices. Identify the competitive force faced by NewGlow Herbals. When is this force evident? How does this force influence the competitive condition of the industry? (1 + 3 + 1 = 5 Marks)
questions.answer: (b)The competitive force faced by NewGlow Herbals is Bargaining Power of Buyers. The bargaining power of buyers is evident when: • Buyers have full knowledge of the sources of products and their substitutes. • Buyers spend a lot of money on the industry’s products , i. e., they are big buyers. • The industry’s product is not perceived as critical to the buyer’s needs, and buyers are more concentrated than the firms supplying the product. They can easily switch to the substitutes available. In the given case, the major supermarket chains and online retail platforms are large and significant buyers of NewGlow Herbals’ products. They can exert pressure on the company to reduce prices as they have the option of replacing its products with cheaper alternative brands . Since customers are highly price sensitive, the retailers can easily threaten to switch to competing brands, thereby strengthening their bargaining position. Influence on Competitive Condition of Industry The bargaining power of buyers influences not only the prices that producers can charge but also, in many cases, the costs and investments of producers , as powerful buyers may demand better services and terms. Thus, strong bargaining power of buyers puts pressure on producers to offer lower prices and better services , which can adversely affect their profitability and the competitive condition of the industry.

(c)NextPro Education Services has gained popularity through its classroom -based professional training programs. The organization is considering entering into international markets through a fully online certification platform. It has experienced faculty members, a strong reputation, and extensive course

content. However, it has limited experience in international operations and online platform management.

The increasing demand for remote learning creates new growth possibilities, while global competition and changing learner preferences present challenges. The management seeks a detailed evaluation before making a strategic decision, through a SWOT analysis approach.

(i)Briefly describe what SWOT Analysis is.

questions.subject: Strategic Management
questions.subTopic: Introduction to Strategic Management - Examination Problem
questions.question: (a)A well- crafted corporate mission not only provides an organisation with its special identity but also serves as a justification for its existence. Elaborate on the primary reasons why an organisation must establish a mission. Furthermore, explain how management expert Peter Drucker advises firms to answer the fundamental question 'what business are we in?' (4 + 1 = 5 Marks)
questions.answer:
(a)Primary reasons why an organisation should have a mission: A mission is an answer to the basic question “What business are we in and what do we do?” It gives an organisation purpose, its own special identity, is unique to the organisation and sets it apart/differentiates it from its competitors. It is central to strategic planning. An organisation should have a mission for the following reasons: • To ensure unanimity of purpose within the organisation. • To develop a basis or standard for allocating organisational resources. • To provide a basis for motivating the use of organisational resources. • To establish a general tone or organisational climate and suggest a business-like operation. • To serve as a focal point for those who identify with the organisation’s purpose and direction. • To facilitate the translation of objectives and goals into a work structure, involving assignment of tasks to responsible elements within the organisation.

• To specify organisational purposes and translate them into goals so that cost, time and performance parameters can be assessed and controlled. According to Peter Drucker , every organisation must ask and correctly answer the fundamental question “What business are we in?” The answer should have a marketing or external perspective rather than merely describing production or generic business activities. A company’s business should be defined in terms of the needs it is trying to satisfy, the customer groups it is targeting and the technologies and competencies it uses.

Thus, the focus should be on the customer need being served rather than merely the product or activity being produced or performed.

questions.subject: Strategic Management
questions.subTopic: Strategic Analysis: Internal Environment - Examination Problem
questions.question:
(b)A company's most profitable business is not receiving the highest investment allocation, while another less profitable business is receiving substantial resources.
Explain how BCG Matrix may justify such a seemingly contrasting decision. (4 + 1 = 5 Marks)
questions.answer:
(b)The BCG Growth -Share Matrix is used for resource allocation in a diversified company. It classifies different businesses or SBUs on the basis of market growth rate and relative market share. Market growth rate indicates market attractiveness, while relative market share indicates the company’s strength in the market. It classifies business units into four categories: stars, cash cows, question marks and dogs. The seemingly contrasting decision of allocating more resources to a less profitable business can be justified as follows: • Cash Cows: These are low -growth, high -market-share businesses. They are established and successful, generate cash and require less investment to maintain their market share. Therefore, a highly profitable business may receive less investment if it is a Cash Cow, as it already generates sufficient cash. • Stars: These are businesses with high market growth and high relative market share. They require heavy investment to maintain their position and finance their rapid growth potential . Therefore, a less profitable business may receive substantial resources if it is a Star, as it represents a good opportunity for expansion. • Question Marks: These are low -market-share businesses in high - growth markets . They require heavy investment and may initially have low potential to generate cash. Investment may be made to increase their market share and turn them into Stars and subsequently Cash Cows.

• Dogs: These are low-growth, low -market-share businesses. They generally have limited future prospects and should be minimised through divestment or liquidation.

Thus, under the BCG Matrix, resource allocation is not based solely on present profitability . A highly profitable Cash Cow may require less investment, whereas a less profitable Star or promising Question Mark may receive greater investment because of its growth potential and future contribution to the organisation.

questions.subject: Strategic Management
questions.subTopic: Introduction to Strategic Management - Examination Problem
questions.question:
(a)A company's success depends on how effectively it manages value creation through various linked activities before the sale, during the sale, and after the sale. Weakness in any one stage can negatively affect the overall customer experience.
Explain this statement using an appropriate strategic framework. (1 + 3 + 1 = 5 Marks)
questions.answer:
(a)The appropriate strategic framework is Value Chain Analysis , developed by Michael Porter. It is a method of examining each activity in the value chain of a business to identify how each stage adds or subtracts value from the end product or service. It helps improve the sequence of operations, enhance efficiency and create competitive advantage. The five primary activities in the value chain are: 1. Inbound Logistics: Activities concerned with receiving, storing and distributing inputs to the product or service, such as material handling, stock control, transportation and warehousing. 2. Operations: Activities that transform inputs into the final product or service, such as machining, packaging, assembly and testing.

3. Outbound Logistics: Activities concerned with collecting, storing and distributing the finished product to customers , including warehousing, material handling and transportation. 4.

Marketing and Sales: Activities through which consumers are made aware of the product or service and are able to purchase it, including advertising, selling and sales administration. 5. Service: Activities that enhance or maintain the value of the product or service, such as installation, repair, training and provision of spares.

These primary activities are supported by procurement, technology development, human resource management and infrastructure. Since the activities are linked and their interactions are a source of competitive advantage, weakness in any one activity can reduce the value delivered to customers and adversely affect the overall customer experience and competitive position.

questions.subject: Strategic Management
questions.subTopic: Introduction to Strategic Management - Examination Problem
questions.question: (b)In today's competitive landscape, effective strategic leaders must deal with rapid, complex changes and diverse competitive situations. Define what constitutes a 'managerial frame of reference' and explain its significance. Furthermore, list any six specific responsibilities of a strategic leader. (2 + 3 = 5 Marks)
questions.answer:
(b)A managerial frame of reference is the set of assumptions, premises and accepted wisdom that bounds a manager’s understanding of the company, the industry in which it competes, and the core competencies that it exploits in pursuit of strategic competitiveness and above - average returns. In other words, it is the foundation on which a manager’s mindset is built. In today’s competitive landscape, strategic leaders must adapt their frames of reference to deal with rapid, complex and diverse competitive situations. Competitive battles are not merely between companies or products, but also between mindsets or managerial frames . Hence, an effective strategic leader must be capable of dealing with cognitively complex situations, change and uncertainty. Responsibilities of a Strategic Leader: 1. Making strategic decisions. 2. Formulating policies and action plans to implement strategic decisions. 3. Ensuring effective communication in the organisation. 4. Managing human capital , which is perhaps the most critical strategic leadership skill.

5. Managing change in the organisation. 6.

Creating and sustaining a strong corporate culture. 7. Sustaining high performance over time.

Thus, strategic leadership skills represent important resources that affect company performance and need to be developed for the company’s future benefit.

questions.subject: Strategic Management
questions.subTopic: Strategic Analysis: Internal Environment - Examination Problem
questions.question:
(a)"A core competency for a firm is whatever it does best."
Explain the concept of core competency. What are the conditions required to be met for a company to regard its competence as core competency? (2 + 3 = 5 Marks)
questions.answer:
(a)A core competency is the collective learning in an organisation, particularly the coordination of diverse production skills and integration of multiple streams of technologies . It is a combination of skills, techniques, resources and capabilities that enables a firm to perform an activity better than its competitors and gain competitive advantage. Thus, a core competency for a firm is “whatever it does best.” According to C. K. Prahalad and Gary Hamel , a competence can be regarded as a core competency when the following three conditions are satisfied:

1. Competitor Differentiation: The competence should be unique and difficult for competitors to imitate .

It should enable the company to perform significantly better than its competitors and sustain its competitive position. 2. Customer Value: The competence should provide a fundamental benefit to customers and have a real impact on their choice to purchase the company’s product or service.

The differentiation offered must be valued by the customer. 3. Application to Other Markets: The competence should be applicable across the organisation and capable of opening up potential markets.

It should not be restricted to one particular skill, product or area of expertise. If these three conditions are met, the company can regard its competence as a core competency.

questions.subject: Strategic Management
questions.subTopic: Introduction to Strategic Management - Examination Problem
questions.question: (b)For any organization undergoing a digital transition, change management is crucial. Define what digital transformation enables an organization to do, and define the process of change management itself. Furthermore, enumerate the five specific ways a properly implemented change management strategy can help an organization, and explain why change management gains more importance in current times. (1 + 3 + 1 = 5 Marks) OR
questions.answer:
(b)Digital transformation is a process of organisational change that enables an organisation to use technology to create new value for customers, employees and other stakeholders. Change management is the process of planning, implementing and monitoring changes in an organisation . It helps organisations achieve their objectives while reducing risks and disruptions. Ways in which Properly Implemented Change Management Helps an Organisation A properly implemented change management strategy can help an organisation to: 1. Specify the parameters and goals of the digital transformation. 2.
Determine which procedures and tools need to be modified. 3. Make a plan for implementing the improvements. 4. Involve staff members and parties involved in the transformation process. 5. Track progress and make required course corrections. Importance of Change Management in Current Times Change management gains more importance in current times because organisations are required to manage new technology, emerging

market opportunities and changing customer preferences . Modern firms must continuously modify their management techniques and approach change in a proactive and organised manner to improve their chances of success.

Thus, change management is a crucial component of digital transformation and helps organisations successfully integrate new digital systems and achieve the intended benefits. Or Strategic Performance Measurement (SPM) is a method that increases line executives’ understanding of an organisation’s strategic goals and provides a continuous system for tracking progress towards these objectives using clear-cut performance measurements.

Strategic Performance Measures and the Insights They Provide Strategic performance measures are key indicators used to track the effectiveness of strategies and support informed decisions regarding resource allocation. They provide the following insights: 1.

Financial Measures: Measures such as revenue growth, Return on Investment (ROI) and profit margins provide an understanding of the organisation’s financial performance and its ability to generate profit. 2. Customer Satisfaction Measures: Measures such as customer satisfaction, customer retention and customer loyalty provide insight into the organisation’s ability to meet customer needs and provide high- quality products and services. 3.

Market Measures: Measures such as market share, customer acquisition and customer referrals provide information about the organisation’s competitiveness in the marketplace and its ability to attract and retain customers. 4. Employee Measures: Measures such as employee satisfaction, turnover rate and employee engagement provide insight into the organisation’s ability to attract and retain talented employees and create a positive work environment.

5. Innovation Measures: Measures such as R&D spending, patent applications and new product launches provide insight into the organisation’s ability to innovate and create new products and services that meet customer needs. 6.

Environmental Measures: Measures such as energy consumption, waste reduction and carbon emissions provide insight into the organisation’s environmental impact and efforts to operate in a sustainable manner. Thus, strategic performance measures provide a snapshot of organisational performance , enabling leaders to assess whether strategies are aligned with goals and objectives and to make necessary adjustments for improved performance. SPM helps to eliminate silos by establishing a common language among all divisions of the organisation, enabling them to communicate openly and productively.

Thus, it promotes better coordination and alignment towards common strategic objectives.
